title: Honey Garlic Pork Tenderloin
seoTitle: Honey Garlic Pork Tenderloin | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Fast grill, glossy glaze, feeds eight
subtitle: Fast grill, glossy glaze, feeds eight
description: Fast grill, glossy glaze, feeds eight. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season and sear
steps.instruction: Pat tenderloins dry; season with salt. Sear in a hot oiled skillet or on the grill 2–3 minutes per side until deeply browned on all sides.

steps.title: Whisk the glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and Dijon mustard until smooth.

steps.title: Finish with the glaze
steps.instruction: Move tenderloins to indirect heat or a 400°F oven. Brush generously with glaze every few minutes, turning, until internal temperature reaches 145°F, about 15–18 minutes.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest tenderloins 5 minutes before slicing into medallions — resting keeps the glaze from washing off and the juices in the meat.

steps.title: Reduce extra glaze and serve
steps.instruction: Simmer any remaining glaze in a small pot 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened; spoon over sliced pork at the line.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Honey Garlic Pork Tenderloin with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Honey Garlic Pork Tenderloin on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Fast grill, glossy glaze, feeds eight. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
